QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_24

question.text: Ms. Sneha Kapoor is exiting a Cat II AIF's 9% stake in Gangotri BioPharma via an IPO. Under the 'Offer for Sale (OFS)' route in an IPO, the exit proceeds to the AIF are realised at:

answer.text: Book value on the company's latest audited balance sheet
The IPO price determined through the book-building/fixed-price process
The first listing-day closing price, irrespective of IPO price

explanation.text: The Logic: When an AIF exits through an Offer for Sale (OFS) in an IPO, it encashes its investment at the IPO price. A partial OFS exit is possible, with the residual stake exited later through the secondary market. The Trap: Face value ignores accumulated value creation. Book value understates the realisable price. Listing-day closing price applies only to subsequent secondary-market exits, not to the OFS leg, which crystallises at the IPO price. Note: ICDR lock-in for pre-IPO shareholders applies as relevant — 6 months or 1 year as applicable under SEBI ICDR — and is not a uniform one-year rule for every situation.
